newsitem.title: CHINA: China launches stockpile information network.
newsitem.headline: China launches stockpile information network.

text.p: China has launched a nationwide information network to help loss-making state-owned firms cut their towering stockpiles of unwanted goods, the Financial News said on Friday.
The Beijing centre of the National Stockpiled Goods Redistribution Network went into operation on May 18, the newspaper said.

The network would help solve the problem of stockpiled goods by allowing them to be traded directly nationwide through the central market in Beijing and later in other large and medium-sized cities, it quoted economic researchers as saying.
Many state-owned enterprises reared under China's old centrally-planned economy have continued to produce huge amounts of largely unwanted goods despite nearly two decades of market-oriented reform.
Economic planners have tried to push companies to focus more on improving their output but have also tried to ease stockpiles by helping such firms find buyers or barter partners for their goods.
The new network would provide information to potential buyers abroad via the Internet worldwide computer network, the Financial News said.

The network was set up by seven ministries, including the Ministry of Internal Trade and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, used advanced information technology, it said but gave no details.

The total value of products stockpiled by Chinese companies had reached 3.0 trillian yuan ($361 billion) by the end of 1996, of which industrial products accounted for 1.3 trillion yuan, it quoted incomplete figures from the State Statistical Bureau as showing.
